title: Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A Cas12a (in4mer) combinatorial knockout screen of 233 cancer-mutated DNA damage response genes, run pairwise in MCF10A and RPE-1 TP53-null cells, yields a genetic interaction map that links previously unconnected DDR pathways and names concrete synthetic lethal pairs: REV1-Pol zeta with MCM8-MCM9-HROB, Fanconi anemia genes with the mitotic repair genes CIP2A, GEN1 and RHNO1, and SMARCAL1 with FANCM and its partners. The retrieved text is a paywalled preview, so the extractable content is the abstract, figure titles, data availability, extended-data legends and author information rather than the full results narrative. All screening data plus AlphaFold-based physical-interaction predictions are released publicly, including GEO accessions and a dedicated database website.

insights.claim: A Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screen disrupted 233 DNA damage response genes that are frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, individually and in pairwise combinations, to measure the phenotypic effect of losing gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Multiplexed Cas12a is maturing into the default engine for pairwise target discovery, supporting the platform thesis behind synthetic-lethality discovery companies.
insights.quote: We disrupt 233 DDR genes frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, either individually or in pairwise combinations

insights.claim: Screening for genetic interactions under unperturbed growth conditions, rather than under added DNA-damaging drug pressure, is enough to surface therapeutically relevant synthetic lethal pairs in the DNA damage response.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Unperturbed screens are cheaper and cleaner than chemogenetic ones, so discovery throughput per dollar in this niche is rising.
insights.quote: enabling us to assess the phenotypic effects induced by the loss of DDR gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth conditions

insights.claim: The pairwise DNA damage response screens were run in two non-transformed human backgrounds, MCF10A breast epithelial cells and RPE-1 TP53-null cells, and reported at an early (t9) and a final (t17/18) time point, with results combined into cell-line integrated datasets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Two independent lines raise confidence in the hit list, but both are non-cancer backgrounds, so tumor-context validation remains a gating step before any hit becomes a drug program.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1 Known single gene

insights.claim: Platform performance was benchmarked by correlating single-gene construct log fold changes against DepMap gene effect scores and by recovering 13 known synthetic lethal paralog control pairs built into the library.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Recovery of known positives is the credibility test that determines whether new pairs from the same screen are worth chasing as targets.
insights.quote: Expected and observed LFCs are plotted with 13 control paralog pairs highlighted in red.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1 Known single gene

insights.claim: Negative interactions called by the pairwise Cas12a screen were compared with previously published CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens in isogenic APEX1-null, APEX2-null and TDP1-null cell lines, with shared hits falling in the top 5% of both approaches.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: One pairwise library can substitute for many separate isogenic knockout screens, compressing the cost and calendar time of DDR target discovery.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1 Known single gene

insights.claim: Overlap of significant genetic interactions between the MCF10A and RPE-1 TP53-null cell lines was reported as Venn diagrams of common versus unique hits at a false discovery rate below 0.1, indicating that a sizeable fraction of DNA damage response interactions is cell-line specific rather than universal.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Context dependence of synthetic lethality is the central commercial risk in this field; single-line hits should be discounted relative to hits replicated across backgrounds.
insights.quote: Venn diagrams displaying the number of common and unique genetic interactions (FDR < 0.1) between MCF10A and RPE-1 TP53−/− cell lines
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1 Known single gene

insights.claim: Significant negative genetic interactions involving essential genes differed between the early and final screen time points, illustrated by module networks for FEN1-LIG1, USP1-WDR48, BOD1L1-ETAA1-POLE3-POLE4 and RAD17-HUS1-RAD9A.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Timing of readout can create or erase an apparent target, so screen duration is a diligence question for any synthetic-lethality dataset being licensed.

insights.claim: All screening data and AlphaFold-based predictions of physical interactions were released through the Supplementary Information and a dedicated public database website, with raw and processed pooled-screen data deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus under accession GSE343308 and END-seq data under GSE343490.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A fully open DDR interaction atlas is free input for every competitor, which lowers barriers to entry and shifts the value from the data itself to downstream chemistry and clinical execution.
insights.quote: All screening data, as well as AlphaFold datasets for the prediction of physical interactions across all integrated datasets, are provided in the Supplementary Information

insights.claim: The computational analysis relied on a newly described regression method, GRAPE (genetic interaction regression analysis of pairwise effects), released as a 2026 preprint, showing that the interpretive layer for combinatorial screens is still being invented alongside the wet-lab platform.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Hit calls depend on unsettled statistical methodology, so results across competing combinatorial-screening platforms are not yet directly comparable.
insights.quote: Analysis of combinatorial knockout CRISPR screens with GRAPE: genetic interaction regression analysis of pairwise effects.
insights.locator: References, Chou, J., Lin, C., Kim, S.

insights.claim: Clustering of the interaction data produced 17 high-confidence gene modules in the MCF10A integrated dataset and 16 in the RPE-1 integrated dataset, with the 233-gene library filtered down to genes participating in top-scoring module-to-module interactions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Module-level dependency maps let developers target a pathway node rather than a single gene, expanding the druggable surface available for a given tumor genotype.
insights.quote: Filtered GI map highlighting genes from 17 high-confidence modules from the MCF10A_integrated dataset.

insights.claim: The genetic interaction map identified connections between DNA damage response pathways that had not previously been linked to each other, in addition to high-confidence positive and negative gene-gene interactions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Newly wired pathway links are where non-obvious combination therapies come from, since they predict vulnerabilities no single-gene screen would nominate.
insights.quote: We identify high-confidence positive and negative gene–gene interactions, along with connections between previously unlinked DDR pathways.

insights.claim: Both buffering (positive) and synthetic lethal (negative) interactions are presented as having therapeutic potential, so the resource is framed as a source of resistance mechanisms as well as kill targets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Buffering interactions predict which second mutations will blunt a DDR drug, which matters for forecasting durability of response and designing combinations up front.
insights.quote: our genetic map of the DDR network identifies synthetic lethal and buffering interactions with therapeutic potential

insights.claim: Module significance was assessed with average genetic interaction z scores against a nominal two-sided P value threshold of 0.1 under a normal approximation, a permissive statistical bar for a discovery map.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Loose significance thresholds mean the map is a hypothesis generator, not a validated target list, so arrayed follow-up is the real cost driver.
insights.quote: corresponding to a nominal two-sided P value ≤ 0.1 under a normal approximation

insights.claim: Hits were prioritized for clinical relevance by mapping deleterious somatic mutations across 134,721 patients in the AACR GENIE database, which flagged 44 of the screened DNA damage response genes as falling in the top 25% of mutated genes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Anchoring synthetic lethal pairs to real-world tumor mutation prevalence converts a screen output into a patient-stratified, addressable-market-sized target list.
insights.quote: The log2-transformed number of patients (n = 134,721) with an assigned deleterious mutation within the coding region of a given gene is shown on the x axis.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2 Identification of cancer-relevant

insights.claim: Mutation prevalence for the 44 cancer-relevant library genes was broken out across 18 cancer types from GENIE, restricted to cancer types with at least 50 patients, giving an indication-by-indication view of where each dependency would apply.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Indication-level prevalence data is what determines whether a biomarker-defined DDR drug has a viable trial population or only a rare-subset niche.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2 Identification of cancer-relevant

insights.claim: Positive (buffering) interactions were separately annotated against ClinVar germline pathogenic variants linked to both cancer and non-cancer disorders, extending the resource from oncology into inherited disease genetics.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Suppressor and modifier interactions in DNA-repair syndromes are an underexploited rare-disease angle that sits adjacent to the oncology franchise.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 3 Identification of disorder-relevant

insights.claim: The screens uncovered synthetic lethality between the genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1-Pol zeta complex and those encoding the MCM8-MCM9-HROB DNA helicase complex, nominated as a targeted-treatment opportunity in tumors mutated for these genes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: MCM8, MCM9 or HROB loss would define a new biomarker-selected population for translesion-synthesis inhibitors, a drug class already in early development.
insights.quote: synthetic lethal interactions between genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1–Pol ζ complex and the MCM8–MCM9–HROB DNA helicase complex

insights.claim: Mechanistic follow-up tied the REV1-MAD2L2-REV3L module to BRCA1 and to the MCM8-MCM9-HROB module using PRIMPOL knockdown, survival assays and electron-microscopy measurement of single-stranded DNA gap lengths at and behind replication forks.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A shared single-stranded-gap mechanism across BRCA1-deficient and MCM8/9-deficient cells would let one translesion-synthesis inhibitor address several genotypes at once.
insights.quote: Quantification of ssDNA gap lengths at and behind replication forks (in nucleotides, nt), detected by EM in MCF10A cells.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 7 Characterization of the negative

insights.claim: Dependence on REV1-Pol zeta was probed with gRNA-resistant REV7 complementation constructs including a REV7 W171A point mutant, separating REV7's translesion-synthesis function from its other roles.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Separation-of-function evidence at a single residue is what makes a protein-protein interface, rather than the whole protein, a tractable small-molecule target.
insights.quote: REV7 W171A mutant cannot be detected with the anti-REV7 antibody because the mutation disrupts the antibody epitope but is detected with an anti-HA antibody.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 7 Characterization of the negative

themes.theme: Fanconi anemia and mitotic DNA repair

insights.claim: The screens found negative interactions between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes, with the validated examples being CIP2A, GEN1 and RHNO1.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Fanconi-pathway-mutant tumors, common in head and neck cancer, gain a specific list of candidate dependencies that are distinct from the crowded PARP target space.
insights.quote: between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes

insights.claim: Loss of GEN1 or CIP2A, alongside APEX2, sensitized RPE-1 TP53-null cells to BRCA1 depletion in survival assays, placing these mitotic repair factors in the same vulnerability class as established BRCA synthetic lethal targets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Additional BRCA1-selective dependencies matter commercially because PARP-inhibitor-resistant BRCA-mutant disease is a large and growing unmet need.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 8 Characterization of the negative

insights.claim: The mechanism was interrogated in a purpose-built U2OS line carrying Halo-tagged polymerase theta and an mNeonGreen knock-in at the RHNO1 locus, imaged live in mitosis after aphidicolin-induced replication stress and CDK1-inhibitor synchronization.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Live-cell readouts of mitotic polymerase theta recruitment give a pharmacodynamic assay that a polymerase theta inhibitor program could adopt directly.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 8 Characterization of the negative

insights.claim: Disruption of FANCL and GEN1 together was assayed for spontaneous CIP2A foci in preanaphase mitotic MCF10A cells, indicating that the lethality runs through unresolved mitotic DNA lesions rather than through interphase repair failure.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If the killing happens in mitosis, drug scheduling relative to the cell cycle becomes a design variable, and mitotic markers become the biomarker to measure.
insights.quote: Quantification of spontaneous CIP2A foci and representative images, respectively, in preanaphase mitotic MCF10A cells upon disruption of FANCL and/or GEN1.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 8 Characterization of the negative

insights.claim: Candidate functional partners for CIP2A, GEN1 and RHNO1 were cross-referenced against top correlated dependencies in DepMap release 24Q4 using Pearson correlation scores, combining the authors' own interaction data with the public cancer dependency map.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Co-dependency correlation on public DepMap data is a near-free triage layer that any team can apply before committing to expensive arrayed validation.
insights.quote: Network representation of top DepMap (24Q4) correlated hits for CIP2A, GEN1, and RHNO1.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 8 Characterization of the negative

insights.claim: Synthetic lethality was identified between the gene encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex, with the interaction extended beyond FANCM itself to its partners such as CENPX.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Mapping the lethality across a whole complex rather than one gene broadens the patient population a SMARCAL1-directed agent could serve.
insights.quote: between genes encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex

insights.claim: SMARCAL1-FANCM double knockout cells showed aberrant anaphases, metaphase DNA breaks and metaphases with cohesion defects plus chromosome fragmentation, pointing to catastrophic mitotic genome instability as the cause of death.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A gross chromosomal-catastrophe phenotype is an easier efficacy readout to run in the clinic than subtle repair-kinetics endpoints.
insights.quote: Quantification of metaphases with cohesion defect and chromosome fragmentation in RPE-1 TP53

insights.claim: The SMARCAL1-FANCM dependency was tested in FaDu head and neck cancer cells with survival assays and western blot confirmation, moving the finding out of engineered non-transformed lines into a human tumor line.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Translation into a tumor line with FANCM-pathway relevance is the step that separates an academic map from an investable target hypothesis.
insights.quote: Western blot showing FANCM and SMARCAL1 levels in FaDu cells examined in survival assays

insights.claim: The authors position their SMARCAL1-FANCM result alongside independently published work reporting profound synthetic lethality between the same two genes, so this pair now has convergent support from separate groups.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Independent replication de-risks SMARCAL1-FANCM relative to the single-paper hits in the same map, which is precisely what moves a target into a funded program.
insights.quote: Profound synthetic lethality between SMARCAL1 and FANCM.

insights.claim: The map also produced suppressor interactions, with DCLRE1B (encoding APOLLO) acting as a suppressor of the non-homologous end joining genes XRCC4, LIG4 and NHEJ1, validated by two-color competition assay and by micronuclei, chromatin bridge, gamma-H2AX and 53BP1 nuclear body readouts.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Suppressor pairs predict which co-occurring lesions will make a DNA-repair-directed drug fail, information needed to write trial exclusion criteria.
insights.quote: Suppressor interactions between DCLRE1B and the NHEJ genes XRCC4, LIG4, and NHEJ1.

insights.claim: APOLLO function was dissected with structure-guided complementation constructs, specifically a deletion of residues 417-532 and an L506E P508A mutant assayed for TRF1 colocalization and rescue of survival, resolving which protein interface carries the phenotype.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Interface-level resolution is what makes a protein-protein interaction chemically tractable rather than merely interesting biology.

insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The underlying data are open in GEO and on the authors' database even though the narrative is paywalled, so the extractable signal sits in the deposited datasets rather than the article.
